name: Jael (Heber's wife)
title: The Woman Who Killed Sisera
summary: Jael was the wife of the Kenite Heber and became famous for killing the Canaanite commander Sisera. She invited the fleeing Sisera into her tent and killed him by driving a tent peg through his temple while he slept. Her courageous act was celebrated in the song of victory sung by Deborah and Barak.

keyEvents.title: Sisera Flees to Jael's Tent
keyEvents.description: After the Israelites defeated the Canaanite army, the commander Sisera fled on foot and came to Jael's tent. She invited him in and gave him milk to drink.

keyEvents.title: Jael Kills Sisera
keyEvents.description: While Sisera slept exhausted, Jael took a tent peg and a hammer and drove the peg through his temple so that he died. This fulfilled Deborah's prophecy that a woman would receive the honor of victory.

keyEvents.title: Jael Shows Barak Sisera's Body
keyEvents.description: When Barak came in pursuit of Sisera, Jael went out to meet him and showed him Sisera lying dead in the tent with the tent peg through his temple.

keyEvents.title: Jael Praised in Deborah's Song
keyEvents.description: In the victory song that Deborah and Barak sang, Jael was praised as the most blessed among women for her courageous act against Sisera.
